nodes.effect: Defines 1119 registered datasets, 1118 mapped normal-class datasets, and 1117 mapped datasets with at least two normal TRAIN rows.

nodes.caller: official router and Exp478 determinism check
nodes.effect: Returns one method from seven numeric TRAIN features using the pinned Exp477 artifact and rules.
Loads normal TRAIN rows, excludes only rows containing non-finite values when at least two clean rows remain, and returns the official method.
Computes the frozen seven TRAIN-only features after the official router excludes non-finite rows.
Must return a singleton equal to the direct official route for all 1117 datasets.
Provides candidate outcomes for the 962 datasets whose AUC and ZF can be evaluated; the other 155 routed datasets do not receive performance claims.
Selects the 1117 population, checks every route, replays 962 scored outcomes, checkpoints progress, and renders HTML.
Preserves completed per-dataset route checks so progress is visible and resumable.
Separates 1117 routing coverage from 962 score-replay performance and records both exclusions.
Shows live progress, final routing coverage, score-replay metrics, exclusions, and checked completed tasks in easy Korean.

constraints: The routing population is exactly 1117 mapped datasets with at least two normal TRAIN rows.
CornellWhaleChallenge is excluded because it is not a normal-class-mapped dataset; Phoneme_normal_39 is excluded because it has one normal TRAIN row.
All 1117 datasets must produce one valid deterministic method and identical feature/direct/pipeline results.
For the 19 missing-value datasets, exactly 164 rows containing 983 NaN or Inf values are excluded without interpolation; finite rows and the frozen feature formulas remain unchanged.
Performance claims use only the 962 frozen score records; the remaining 155 datasets receive routing coverage claims only.
Dataset names locate database rows and identify report entries but are not policy features.
The database, official sources, Exp474 through Exp477 results, and frozen checkpoints remain read-only.
No new score source or dense tensor stage is introduced, so MLX assessment is not applicable.
